mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market strengthening indicated by unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4.5% signals improving consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where UNRATE is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates robust consumer demand and labor market strength, signaling accelerating corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL and PAYEMS increase by at least 0.1% and 0.5% respectively over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During the post-recession recovery phase, a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a rebound in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes improved corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months during the post-recession recovery period when INDPRO rises by at least 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500,000 units signals strong consumer confidence and construction activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST exceeds 1500.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust consumer and business demand, which typically leads to sustained corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS and INDPRO both increase by at least 0.5% and 0.3% respectively over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates economic stress from restrictive policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months during a monetary tightening cycle when UNRATE rises by at least 0.2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects expanding manufacturing output, which typically precedes higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where INDPRO increases by at least 0.5%.
